author: DPA
title: Pets can get sunburn too. How to protect them when the weather is hot - NewsBreak
text:
56 minutes ago
Avoid long walks and extended swimming trips on particularly hot days for dogs as beyond sunburn, dogs are also at risk of heatstroke and sunstroke. Karl-Josef Hildenbrand/dpa Too much sun can take its toll on our pets. You can spot first indications of sunburn through reddened, painful skin.
Next may come itching. If your pet scratches their damaged skin, this can cause further harm and in the worst case, lead to infections.
Animals that have recently been shorn or have short, white coats – such as Dalmatians and Bull Terriers – are particularly prone to sunburn. They have far more sensitive skin so need special protection from intense sunlight.
Veterinarian Tina Hölscher from German animal welfare organization Aktion Tier advises dog owners to avoid long walks and extended swimming trips on particularly hot days. This is because, as well as sunburn, dogs are also at risk of heatstroke and sunstroke.
Well protected in the sun
If you cannot avoid direct sunlight, particularly sensitive areas of your pets' skin such as the bridge of the nose or the ears need extra protection.
Ideally, use a waterproof sun cream with a high sun protection factor. You can find them specifically for dogs and cats.
Otherwise, it’s best to avoid the sunlight altogether. If you head to parks or outdoor areas, it’s best to find a spot in the shade to lie down with your four-legged friend. Cooling off in the water can also help prevent them from overheating.
Medicines an underestimated risk
Many of us fail to realise that certain medicines can make skin more sensitive to light, for both humans and animals. That increases the risk of sunburn. Watch out for diabetes tablets and certain antibiotics, among others.
If animals are taking such medicines, try to avoid intense sunlight wherever possible. Otherwise you may see their skin responding with redness and swelling, even after only being briefly exposed to UV rays.
Pets get sunburn too. You can apply protective cream to sensitive areas and ensure your animals get enough water and shade if it is warm where you are. Martin Gerten/dpa/dpa-tmn Protect your pets from the sun when the weather is hot by providing shade. Some medicines may make pets more sensitive to light. You can also apply protective cream to parts of a dog's nose for example. Martin Gerten/dpa 1
